title: Run the human review pilot (6 reviewers, paired patches); first rebuild both ccmanager trees at 46fe720 durably, then design the 3 other claims
notes: on strict vs original patches; a lighter cap/complexity/boundary gate
against the full structural gate; first-run adoption on clean fixtures;
per-rule false-positive rate in report-only mode. Smallest step: design
the human review pilot (6-10 reviewers, paired patches).

2026-11-23: the human review pilot is pre-registered in docs/evidence/2026-10-30-human-review-pilot-design.md, with a second review applied (noncentral-t sample size, zero-variance detection interval, unavailable sensitivity model). Nothing can run until the owner decides: whether to recruit 6, 8 or 10 reviewers and who, and who the two blinded scorers are. The other three claims (lighter gate, first-run adoption, per-rule false-positive rate) are not designed.

2026-11-23, owner answer to the recruiting question: "lo que veas y usa codex" (decide yourself, use Codex). Decision: six reviewers (R1-R6), the smallest table, and Codex generates the patch pairs. Reading "use Codex" as Codex also playing the reviewers and scorers is my interpretation, not confirmed; a run like that measures agent review, not the human claim, and must be reported under that label. Blocker found the same day: the October material (measure3/v3/t5: 20 task statements, frozen hidden tests, both ccmanager trees) lived in a session scratchpad that no longer exists, and no copy was found on disk or on GitHub. The design covers this: write eight new tasks, freeze their hidden tests, report the deviation. The strict tree (one exported unit per file, 1342 files) has to be rebuilt first. Next step: rebuild both trees at 46fe720 in a durable directory outside /tmp.
